# Locality Guide: Bohemia (1800–1830)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** +1002 as Kingdom of Bohemia; Habsburg Austrian Crown Land during this period
- **Administrative center:** Prague (Praha)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Habsburg Austrian Empire
- **Economy:** Agriculture, linen weaving, glass; industrialization beginning 1820s
- **Ethnic composition:** Czech-speaking majority; large German-speaking minority in western/northern border districts
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic (dominant); Lutheran/Evangelical (permitted from 1781); Jewish (required under Catholic supervision from 1784)
- **Key events:** 1781 Toleration Patent; 1784 standardized church records; 1815 Congress of Vienna; 1820s industrial revolution

## Boundary changes
Stable Crown Land borders throughout 1800–1830. All registers centralized into Czech state regional archives in the 1950s.

## Available record types

### Church records (primary vital record source)
- **Baptism entries (1784+):** child's name; parents' full names, grandparents' names, towns of origin, house/conscription number; standardized columnar format
- **Languages:** Latin, Czech, German; Gothic/Old German script pre-1850
- **Where held:** Seven Czech state regional archives
- **FamilySearch access:** CID 1804263 (indexed + images); CID 1472854 Southern Bohemia browse-only; CID 1784129 legacy index

### Civil registration
- **None before 1869** — church records are the sole vital records source for 1800–1830

### Census records
- No census for 1800–1830 period; earliest FamilySearch census records begin 1843 (CID 1930345)

### Land records
- Czech Republic Land Records, 1450-1889 (FamilySearch, browse-only)

## Repository guide

| Repository | Collection | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | CID 1804263 (Church Books, 1552-1981) — indexed + images | Free |
| FamilySearch | CID 1472854 (Southern Bohemia Třeboň, 1650-1900) — browse-only | Free |
| FamilySearch | CID 1784129 (Births & Baptisms, 1637-1889) — index only | Free |
| Ancestry | Czech Republic Church Books 1552-1963 (col. 60254) | Subscription |
| digi.ceskearchivy.cz | Třeboň DigiArchiv — Southern Bohemia | Free |
| vademecum.soalitomerice.cz | Litoměřice — Northern Bohemia | Free |
| ebadatelna.soapraha.cz | Prague Regional — Central Bohemia | Free |
| aron.vychodoceskearchivy.cz | Zámrsk — Eastern Bohemia | Free |

## Research tips
1. Identify the specific parish first using GenTeam Gazetteer (genteam.at)
2. Search CID 1804263 indexed collection for Agnes Michl / Anežka Michlová with parents
3. Also search legacy index CID 1784129 and Ancestry col. 60254
4. Pre-1850 Gothic script requires paleographic skill — use FamilySearch 'Reading Czech Parish Registers' course
5. Czech feminine suffix -ová: search both Michl and Michlová, Findejs and Findejsová
6. No civil registration before 1869; all births are church records

## Probable Conclusion: Agnes (b. 1 March 1818, Svitavy, Moravia) Is a Daughter of Maxmilián Michl and Anna [Findejsová]

**Research question:** Does any baptismal or birth record document a daughter named Agnes born approximately 1818 to Maxmilián Michl (b. ca. 1795) and Anna Marie Findejsová (b. 13 March 1784, Bystré, Bohemia)?

**Geographic note:** The original research question specified Bohemia. The baptism records locate the Michl family at Svitavy (German: Zwittau), a market town in the Moravská Třebová district of Moravia — historically across the Bohemia–Moravia provincial border. Svitavy was part of the Czech Crown Lands (Habsburgische Erblande) in 1818. The question is answered affirmatively for Moravia.

---

### Evidence

**Record 1 — Agnes baptism (direct evidence)**

"Czech Republic, Church Books, 1552-1981," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6PJZ-ZB9V : accessed 9 August 2026), entry for Agnes and Maxmilian Michal, 1 Mar 1818; citing Moravia, Religious records, image volume https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89S1-K869.

This indexed entry in FamilySearch collection CID 1804263 records the baptism of a female infant named Agnes on 1 March 1818 at Svitavy, Moravská Třebová, Moravia, with her birth also on the same date. The father is indexed as "Maxmilian Michal" and the mother as "Anna." Source classification: **derivative** (FamilySearch index/abstract of the original Catholic parish register); **primary** information (recorded contemporaneously by persons with direct knowledge: the presenting parents and officiating priest); **direct** evidence (the entry explicitly names Agnes as the daughter of the identified father). The original register image is accessible at ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89S1-K869; it was attempted but could not be reliably read due to image-size limitations with the OCR tools available. This finding rests on the derivative index.

**Record 2 — Anna baptism (corroborating)**

"Czech Republic, Church Books, 1552-1981," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6PJZ-CTT9 : accessed 9 August 2026), entry for Anna, daughter of Maxmilian and Anna Michl, baptism 17 Sep 1823, Svitavy, Moravská Třebová, Moravia; citing original parish register image at https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:HQHL-KQSY (image volume: https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-89S1-K8F7).

This indexed entry records the baptism of Anna, daughter of Maxmilian Michl and his wife Anna, on 17 September 1823 at the same Svitavy parish. It corresponds to the known tree person P91P-VCD (Anna Michlová, b. 16 Sep 1823), the couple's previously documented daughter, and was already attached to P915-SXM in the FamilySearch collaborative tree. It establishes that the Michl family was resident at Svitavy and entering baptisms in this Catholic register in the same era, providing the geographic anchor that identifies the Agnes 1818 entry as belonging to the same family. Classification: **derivative** source, **primary** information, **direct** evidence for Anna's birth, **indirect** corroborating evidence for Agnes's parentage.

---

### Correlation and analysis

**Father identification:** The Agnes entry indexes the father as "Maxmilian Michal"; the Anna entry uses "Maxmilian Michl." These represent an established Czech/German transliteration variant — "Michal" is the standard Czech rendering of the German "Michl" by indexers of Moravian registers. A FamilySearch same-person algorithmic comparison of the Agnes entry's father persona against P915-SXM returned a match score of 0.889 (strong, above the 0.7 threshold); the same comparison against the Anna entry's father returned 0.895. The Anna 1823 record was already attached to P915-SXM in the FamilySearch collaborative tree before this research, providing independent confirmation that P915-SXM is the Svitavy-parish Maxmilian Michl. The surname variation is an expected indexing artifact.

**Mother identification:** Both entries record the mother only as "Anna," without a maiden name. No marriage record for Maxmilián Michl and Anna Marie Findejsová was located during this research. Identification of P915-7QP (Anna Marie Findejsová) as the mother rests on family-unit reasoning: the same father (P915-SXM) appears at the same parish in both records, and P915-7QP is the recorded spouse of P915-SXM. This identification is probable but not independently confirmed from these index records alone. A direct document naming "Findejsová" as the mother — such as the parents' marriage record, a census listing, or the full text of the original register images — would strengthen it. These remain unsearched or not-yet-read sources.

**Agnes's surname:** Agnes's given name alone appears in the index. Standard Czech feminine naming practice gives daughters the feminized form of the father's surname; the expected surname would be "Michlová," consistent with her sister Anna being recorded as "Anna Michlová." No surname for Agnes is asserted from this source.

---

### Collateral discrepancy

The known daughter P91P-VCD (Anna Michlová, b. 1823) carries a pre-existing birth-place entry of "Bystré/Bistrau, Polička, Bohemia" that conflicts with the baptism register's "Svitavy, Moravská Třebová, Moravia." This discrepancy is collateral to the Agnes question. The register evidence (primary, direct) outweighs the unsourced pre-existing tree value. Both values coexist in the tree pending formal correction.

---

### Research scope

Searches covered FamilySearch indexed collection CID 1804263 using Agnes/Anežka with Michl/Michlová; the father's name Maxmilian/Maximilianus Michl/Michal without record-type restriction; and the mother's surname Findejs/Findejsová. The legacy index CID 1784129 was also searched. A marriage search in CID 1804263 and CID 1804227 yielded no couple-marriage record. The original register images for both identified records were attempted but not reliably read. An Ancestry search and a full-text co-occurrence search were planned as fallbacks but were not needed. Direct examination of the original register images and a search for the parents' marriage record remain as the primary steps to advance this conclusion.

---

### Tier declaration

**Probable.** The evidence strongly suggests that Agnes, baptized 1 March 1818 at Svitavy, Moravia, is a daughter of Maxmilián Michl (P915-SXM) and Anna [Findejsová] (P915-7QP). The conclusion does not reach the proved tier because: (1) both records are derivative index entries whose original images have not been independently examined; (2) both records derive from the same underlying parish register; and (3) the mother's maiden name "Findejsová" has not been confirmed by a record that directly names her in connection with Agnes. Proof would require reading the original register images and locating at least one additional independent source naming both parents in connection with this child.

*Previously unknown evidence may alter this assessment.*

# Locality Guide: Bohemia (1800–1830)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** +1002 as Kingdom of Bohemia; a hereditary Crown Land of the Habsburg Austrian Empire during this period
- **Administrative center:** Prague (Praha)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Habsburg Austrian Empire
- **Population during period:** No FamilySearch population data returned for this standardPlace/period; according to historical records Bohemia had roughly 3–4 million inhabitants in the early 19th century
- **Economy:** Agriculture, linen weaving, glass manufacture; beginning of industrial revolution in Bohemia in the 1820s (per FS wiki Czechia History timeline)
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Czech-speaking; large German-speaking minority (especially in western and northern border districts); small Jewish communities in towns
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic overwhelming majority; Protestant registers permitted under Catholic supervision from 1781; Jewish registers required from 1784 under Catholic supervision; separate Protestant registers legal from 1840
- **Key historical events:** Habsburg Joseph II's 1781 Toleration Patent; 1784 standardized church record law; 1805 Battle of Slavkov; 1815 Treaty of Vienna; 1820s industrial revolution begins in Bohemia

## Boundary changes
- Stable Crown Land borders during this period (1800–1830) — no boundary changes affecting the archival jurisdiction.
- Records are filed at the parish level and collected by district, then regional archive (Krajský archiv); in the 1950s all registers were centralized into Czech state regional archives.
- Since 1993 the modern entity is "Czechia / Czech Republic" but records remain in the same physical archives under the same organization.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** 1869 — civil registration did not begin until Austrian law of 1869.
- **What exists for 1800–1830:** None — all vital records in this period are church records.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers (matriky) are the legal equivalents for this period and cover virtually the entire population.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Roman Catholic (primary); Lutheran/Evangelical (permitted under Catholic supervision from 1781); Jewish (required under Catholic supervision from 1784)
- **Record types:** Baptisms (křty), marriages (oddavky), burials (pohřby), and indexes. From 1784, standardized columnar format includes: child's name, parents' full names, grandparents' names, towns of origin, house number/military conscription number. From 1790, separate indexes required by law; from 1802, older registers had to be indexed.
- **Languages:** Latin, Czech, German (depending on year and priest); Gothic/Old German script for entries before ca. 1850 — requires paleographic skill to read
- **Where held:** Seven Czech state regional archives, organized by district. For Bohemia:
  - **Northern Bohemia:** Litoměřice Regional Archives (vademecum.soalitomerice.cz)
  - **Southern Bohemia:** Třeboň Regional Archives (digi.ceskearchivy.cz)
  - **Central/West Bohemia around Prague:** Prague (Praha) Regional Archives (ebadatelna.soapraha.cz) and Prague City Archives
  - **Western Bohemia:** Plzeň Regional Archives (portafontium.eu)
  - **Eastern Bohemia:** Zámrsk Regional Archives (aron.vychodoceskearchivy.cz)
- **Digitization:** FamilySearch has digitized and indexed many registers from Litoměřice, Třeboň, Opava, and Zámrsk archives in collection **Czech Republic, Church Books, 1552-1981** (CID 1804263) — **indexed + images**. Additional Southern Bohemia records are in **Czech Republic, Southern Bohemia, Třeboň Archive Church Books, 1650-1900** (CID 1472854) — **browse-only images** (0 indexed records). The legacy index-only collection **Czech Republic, Births and Baptisms, 1637-1889** (CID 1784129) covers some records not in 1804263.
- **Volume inventory:** FamilySearch volume_search returned **28,065 volumes** covering Bohemia in 1800–1830. The overwhelming majority are **browse-only** (recordSearchablePercent = 0, fulltextSearchable = false). A small subset have recordSearchablePercent = 100 (name-indexed). Browsing without a specific parish is impractical — identify the parish first.

### Census records
- **No census during this period.** The first FamilySearch-accessible Czech census records begin 1843 (collection 1930345, Czech Republic Censuses and Inhabitant Registers, 1800-1990 — images, from Northern Bohemia/Litoměřice, Eastern Bohemia/Trutnov, Southern Bohemia/Třeboň, Southern Moravia/Brno, Northern Moravia/Opava, and Zámrsk).
- **Parish soul registers (soupisy duší):** Some parishes maintained periodic household status registers ("status animarum") which enumerate household members — these are not systematic but survive for some parishes and are browsable via the same archives.
- **Conscription records:** From 1784, baptism entries record the father's military conscription number (konskripční číslo) and house number — useful for identifying the exact village.

### Probate and court records
- Estate and court records exist for this period in regional archives. Not the primary tool for birth questions but can supply contextual information. Not well-indexed online.

### Land records
- **FamilySearch:** Czech Republic Land Records, 1450-1889 (browse-only images at FamilySearch; also on Ancestry subscription)

### Military records
- Not directly relevant for an 1818 birth question. Austrian conscription affected males; father's conscription number appears in baptism entries.

### Cemetery records
- Cemetery stones from this period rarely survive, and Czech cemeteries have limited online coverage (czech.stonepics.com for some). Not a primary source for an 1818 baptism.

### School records
- **Czech Republic School Registers, 1799-1953** at FamilySearch (CID 2328519) — browse-only images. Earliest coverage overlaps the period; not useful for birth confirmation.
